the application of the TACT reconstruction method to digital mammograms yields significantly higher detection scores than conventional 2D spot mammography.

the application of 3D imaging techniques to the detection of microcalcifications in mammography, and the purpose of this paper is to describe the design of our experiments and the preliminary results obtained.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

TACT is a more effective display medium than 2D digital imaging for the detection of microcalcifications and masses in the presence of dense tissue, and that the effect is robust with regard to observer and exposure.
TACT is a superior method for detection of low-contrast objects in digital mammography.
TACT is a superior method of imaging the breast compared with conventional digital mammography for all tasks simulated in this study.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TACT is a promising alternative to conventional 2-dimensional digital mammography for the detection of low-contrast objects in breast tissue.
TACT has the potential to improve the detection accuracy of breast cancer.
TACT is a potentially valuable adjunct or replacement to conventional 2-dimensional digital mammography.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the TACT reconstruction method can be used to generate 3D displays of digital mammography data that are superior to conventional 2-dimensional mammograms for certain tasks.
